newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE nearby canola ends up on Japan, commercials.
newsitem.headline: WCE nearby canola ends up on Japan, commercials.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed mixed, with nearby contracts higher on Japanese and commerical demand late in the day, traders said.

"UGG, RBC-DS and the Japanese bought July late. Cargill bought 300 November. Locals and commission houses sold," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin fell to -12.99 Tuesday from -9.55 Monday. About 300 July-Aug spread $0.50, 600 July-Nov $35 as RBC-DS bought, Aug-Sep $30.30. Volume was 5,142 lots, or 102,840 tonnes, with 225 hedge lots.
Japan bought 5,000-6,000 tonnes of canola overnight, sources said.
July canola futures closed up $2.50 at $402.70 and November ended down $0.80 at $366.80. July flax up $2.50 to $331, November up $2 to $315.
RBC-DS sold 200 July-Sep flax spread at $15. Volume 620.
"Dry weather concerns are starting to show up," a trader said. The Canadian Wheat Board said Monday the Prairies faced a potential drought if significant rain did not fall soon.
July western barley fell $0.50 to $131 on commercial liquidation and October closed down $0.30 at $133.10. Alberta Wheat Pool sold 300 July-Oct at $2. Volume was 1,085 lots.

July wheat lost $0.50, closing at $156.10 on hedges. December fell $1.30 to $158.20 on local sales. AWP sold 50 July-Oct at $2 to PCTS, a trader said. Volume was 358 lots. Oats did not trade. PCTS sold 30 October peas down US$0.30 to US$182.70 to RBC, traders said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
